summary:
Held 1 of today's 10 biggest UK/EU movers.

• 5 upside misses — NG.L +3%, SVT.L +3%, BA.L +3%, SSE.L +2%, SHEL.L +2%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (BRBY.L -6%, PRX.AS -5%, BESI.AS -5%, IMCD.AS -4%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: BRBY.L (-6.38%) — Q1 FY27 update (Jul 17) beat on sales (+5% comp, all 4 divisions positive) but cautious geopolitical/macro guidance and EMEIA -3% tourist weakness triggered a multi-day sell-off into Jul 20. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe — BRBY.L is a UK-listed luxury/apparel retailer (FTSE 100, GBp-denominated), a sector/region combo the bot's uk-eu universe screen likely doesn't cover, so no filter ever saw it, let alone excluded it on signal grounds.

top_movers.catalyst: No dated news catalyst found for 2026-07-20; National Grid's last scheduled events were FY results (14 May) and RIIO-T3 acceptance — likely a rate-sensitive/defensive sector move.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — NG.L is a large-cap UK regulated utility with structurally low beta/ATR, a profile momentum/gainer screens typically exclude even though today's 3.33% move is unusually large for the name.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a low-beta/defensive-utility bucket to the uk-eu universe with a relaxed inclusion rule: admit names when daily move exceeds 2x their 20-day ATR, even if baseline beta/volatility falls below the standard momentum floor.

top_movers.catalyst: Defensive rotation into tobacco during a tech-sector selloff, amplified by BAT's disclosed closed-period share buyback (up to 217.5M shares) running through July 29 ahead of July 30 H1 results.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — BATS.L is a FTSE 100 defensive/tobacco name, a sector category likely excluded from growth/momentum-focused universes. Only macro-aligned-macro-attn, which tracks sector-rotation/defensive-flow signals, held it.
top_movers.suggestion: Add FTSE 100 defensive/tobacco names to other strategies' universes, or add a buyback-RNS signal flagging stocks with disclosed closed-period buybacks as low-risk momentum candidates.

top_movers.catalyst: No single-name news; sector-wide UK water-utility rally (SVT +2.89%, peers UU/NG/SSE also up 2-3%) tracking falling gilt yields and BoE rate-cut expectations — a bond-proxy rotation.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — SVT.L is a defensive, low-beta FTSE 100 regulated utility, a category momentum/news-reactive bots typically exclude in favor of higher-volatility, higher-volume names.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a macro rate-proxy screen (trigger on 10Y gilt yield move ≥15bps) that temporarily admits FTSE bond-proxy utilities (water/National Grid/SSE) into a mean-reversion sleeve during rate-driven sector rotations.

top_movers.catalyst: Sector-wide defense re-rating: Germany/Italy raising defense budgets pre-NATO summit, Kepler upgrade to Buy, Erste Group lifted FY26 EPS ahead of July 30 H1 results.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — BAE Systems is a large-cap aerospace/defense name; bot's uk-eu universe likely applies an ESG/defense-sector exclusion screen rather than a cap or liquidity filter.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a defense/aerospace carve-out or separate sector universe (e.g. `uk_eu_defense_watchlist`) so sector-driven rallies like the NATO-spending re-rating aren't fully excluded by the ESG screen.

top_movers.catalyst: No single-day news catalyst found; move likely reflects continued re-rating on Ofgem RIIO-T3/ED3 regulatory clarity plus a sector-wide defensive/utility rotation as gilt yields eased.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — SSE.L is a FTSE 100 large-cap UK regulated utility/renewables name, a low-beta, dividend-defensive sector the bot's momentum/news-reactive screens don't cover at all.
top_movers.suggestion: Add FTSE 100 regulated-utility names (market cap > £10B) as a dedicated defensive/sector-rotation universe slice so regulatory-driven re-ratings like Ofgem price-control settlements are captured.

top_movers.catalyst: Brent crude spiked above $90/bbl on renewed US-Iran military escalation and Strait of Hormuz supply threats, lifting Shell alongside BP and other majors.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — SHEL.L is a large-cap UK integrated energy major, likely excluded because current strategies focus on other sectors/caps and don't carry an oil & gas / geopolitical-risk sleeve.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a UK/EU large-cap energy sub-universe (SHEL.L, BP.L) gated on a Brent-crude daily-move trigger (e.g. >3% move) so geopolitically-driven oil rallies become tradable signals.

top_movers.catalyst: Q1 FY27 update (Jul 17) beat on sales (+5% comp, all 4 divisions positive) but cautious geopolitical/macro guidance and EMEIA -3% tourist weakness triggered a multi-day sell-off into Jul 20.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — BRBY.L is a UK-listed luxury/apparel retailer (FTSE 100, GBp-denominated), a sector/region combo the bot's uk-eu universe screen likely doesn't cover, so no filter ever saw it, let alone excluded it on signal grounds.
top_movers.suggestion: Add FTSE 100 luxury-goods/apparel names to the uk-eu universe screen, or add a post-earnings-drift rule flagging names with cumulative 3-day move beyond -8% after a trading update for mean-reversion review.

top_movers.catalyst: No single-day trigger; continuation of multi-day slide from global tech/Tencent-linked selloff (AI-competition jitters) plus forced Delivery Hero-to-Uber stake-sale overhang and failed technical breakout.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — PRX.AS is a Netherlands-domiciled holding company (Tencent proxy) on Euronext Amsterdam, a non-US large-cap conglomerate listing that falls outside the sector/cap buckets the bot's uk-eu universe currently tracks.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap EU holding/conglomerate tickers with high China-proxy correlation (PRX.AS, and flag Tencent 0700.HK co-movement) to the uk-eu universe so sector-wide Asia-tech selloffs get sized even without a discrete headline.

top_movers.catalyst: Broad EU chip-equipment selloff (ASML, ASM Intl both ~-6% on AI-capex sustainability jitters) layered on Besi's own hybrid-bonding delay overhang (Samsung/SK Hynix reconsidering adoption timeline) ahead of its July 23 earnings.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: BESI.AS is a Euronext Amsterdam semiconductor-equipment large-cap (~€17.5B) not in the uk-eu sector coverage; even if covered, a pre-earnings blackout (report due July 23, 3 trading days out) would likely have excluded it anyway.
top_movers.suggestion: Add EU semiconductor-equipment peers (ASML, ASM International, BESI.AS) to the uk-eu momentum universe, and let a sector-selloff rule override the pre-earnings blackout when the move tracks a peer-group gap of ≥5% same-day.

top_movers.catalyst: No single-day news trigger found — extends a ~10% one-month downtrend amid Q1 margin-pressure concerns, likely de-risking ahead of July 29 H1 earnings.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — IMCD.AS is a ~€5B Euronext Amsterdam specialty-chemicals distributor (AEX-listed mid-cap), a sector/exchange combo the uk-eu universe screens don't currently cover.
top_movers.suggestion: Extend uk-eu universe cap/exchange filter to include Euronext Amsterdam AEX constituents ≥€3B mkt cap so blue-chip mid-caps like IMCD are screened, not just FTSE/DAX/CAC names.
